policy.version_rule: Prefer the target repository's pinned versions and CI matrix; otherwise verify the current official release or pin an official source revision.
policy.selection_rule: Query by bottleneck and platform, inspect project-native infrastructure first, and install only the selected compatible stack.

entries.name: NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit and binary utilities
entries.use_when: Compile CUDA C++, inspect PTX/SASS/resource usage, or provide NVCC for TileLang/CUTLASS JIT paths.

entries.name: CUDA Python
entries.use_when: Drive CUDA runtime/driver APIs, compilation, and device operations directly from Python.

entries.name: CUTLASS and CuTe DSL
entries.use_when: Need architecture-specific tensor-core GEMM/attention pipelines, epilogues, TMA, warp specialization, or Blackwell control.

entries.name: NVIDIA cuTile Python
entries.use_when: Evaluate NVIDIA's tile-programming Python path when the installed CUDA release and target GPU are explicitly supported.

entries.name: cuDNN Frontend
entries.use_when: Use cuDNN graph APIs or open-source frontend kernels before writing custom attention/convolution/normalization infrastructure.

entries.name: cuBLASLt
entries.use_when: Need tuned matmul algorithms, layouts, scaling, FP8/FP4/quantized modes, or fused epilogues without owning a custom GEMM.

entries.name: CUDA Core Compute Libraries (CCCL: Thrust, CUB, libcudacxx)
entries.use_when: Reuse production reductions, scans, sorting, iterators, and CUDA C++ primitives instead of rebuilding them.

entries.name: NVIDIA Transformer Engine
entries.use_when: Optimize transformer training/inference with supported FP8/FP4, fused normalization, attention, and linear layers.

entries.name: NVIDIA MatX
entries.use_when: Build composed C++ GPU numerical pipelines using reusable transforms rather than individual handwritten kernels.

entries.name: NVIDIA NVTX
entries.use_when: Annotate phases, kernels, streams, and iteration boundaries for Nsight traces.

entries.name: PyTorch custom operators and torch.library
entries.use_when: Register custom kernels with autograd, fake/meta tensors, torch.compile, opcheck, and stable PyTorch APIs.

entries.name: torch.compile and TorchInductor
entries.use_when: Check whether compiler fusion/codegen already solves the graph before adding a custom kernel, and ensure custom ops compose with compile.

entries.name: Triton
entries.use_when: Implement portable high-performance custom operators with explicit program tiling and compiler autotuning.

entries.name: Triton Gluon
entries.use_when: Need more explicit layouts, shared-memory movement, and architecture-specific control inside the Triton ecosystem.

entries.name: TileLang
entries.use_when: Use tile-level Python kernel construction, TMA/tensor-core pipelines, and fast architecture-focused prototyping when the project supports it.

entries.name: PyTorch Helion
entries.use_when: Evaluate a higher-level Python-embedded kernel DSL that autotunes schedules while retaining PyTorch integration.

entries.name: ThunderKittens
entries.use_when: Build NVIDIA kernels from reusable tile primitives when low-level CUDA control is required.

entries.name: Apache TVM
entries.use_when: Use compiler scheduling, tensor IR, autotuning, and multi-backend code generation for operator or graph-level work.

entries.name: FlagGems
entries.use_when: Reuse or study a broad Triton operator library before implementing common LLM operators again.

entries.name: FlashAttention
entries.use_when: Use or compare against maintained exact-attention kernels before implementing dense attention from scratch.

entries.name: FlashInfer
entries.use_when: Optimize LLM serving attention, KV-cache, sampling, and fused inference operators.

entries.name: xFormers
entries.use_when: Reuse composable optimized transformer blocks and attention implementations.

entries.name: Liger Kernel
entries.use_when: Reuse memory-efficient Triton kernels for LLM training losses, norms, MLPs, and model integrations.

entries.name: DeepGEMM
entries.use_when: Study or reuse high-performance low-precision dense/grouped GEMM kernels, especially MoE paths.

entries.name: FlashMLA
entries.use_when: Implement or compare Multi-head Latent Attention decode/prefill kernels.

entries.name: causal-conv1d
entries.use_when: Reuse fused causal depthwise Conv1D kernels used by state-space models.

entries.name: Mamba SSM kernels
entries.use_when: Reuse/selective-scan and SSD/state-space kernels before reproducing the architecture's core operators.

entries.name: Flash Linear Attention
entries.use_when: Reuse shared linear-attention, recurrent, delta-rule, sparse-attention, and SSM kernels/backends.

entries.name: NVIDIA Apex
entries.use_when: Use supported fused optimizers, normalization, mixed precision, and distributed training extensions.

entries.name: Marlin
entries.use_when: Study FP16xINT4 inference GEMM layouts and kernels, while checking whether the target serving stack has a maintained fork.

entries.name: bitsandbytes
entries.use_when: Reuse k-bit quantization, optimizers, and linear layers instead of building common quantized training primitives.

entries.name: torchao
entries.use_when: Use PyTorch-native quantization and sparsity flows and kernels.

entries.name: FBGEMM_GPU
entries.use_when: Reuse production quantized GEMM, embedding, sparse, and GenAI kernels.

entries.name: TensorRT-LLM
entries.use_when: Optimize full LLM inference engines and inspect integrated NVIDIA kernels before local micro-optimization.

entries.name: vLLM
entries.use_when: Measure kernel impact in a real high-throughput serving engine and reuse its attention/quantization operator integrations.

entries.name: SGLang
entries.use_when: Validate kernels in a production serving runtime and inspect its optimized backend integrations.

entries.name: NVIDIA NCCL
entries.use_when: Use optimized collectives and diagnose multi-GPU communication before implementing custom communication kernels.

entries.name: NCCL Tests
entries.use_when: Establish communication baselines and topology effects independently of the model stack.

entries.name: NVIDIA NVSHMEM
entries.use_when: Need one-sided or kernel-initiated multi-GPU communication and fine-grained synchronization.

entries.name: MSCCL++
entries.use_when: Build GPU-driven custom collective/point-to-point communication schedules for scalable AI workloads.

entries.name: DeepEP
entries.use_when: Optimize expert-parallel dispatch/combine communication for MoE training and inference.

entries.name: Triton-distributed
entries.use_when: Explore compiler-supported distributed kernels that fuse communication with computation.

entries.name: NVIDIA Nsight Compute
entries.use_when: Inspect kernel-level counters, occupancy, memory traffic, instruction mix, roofline, and stall reasons.

entries.name: NVIDIA Nsight Systems
entries.use_when: Locate CPU launch overhead, synchronization, stream gaps, communication overlap, and multi-process timeline bottlenecks.

entries.name: NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer
entries.use_when: Run memcheck, racecheck, initcheck, and synccheck on CUDA kernels.

entries.name: CUDA Profiling Tools Interface (CUPTI)
entries.use_when: Build custom profiler/trace integrations or understand the data source behind PyTorch/Nsight tooling.

entries.name: NVBench
entries.use_when: Create statistically sound CUDA C++ microbenchmarks with device-aware measurements.

entries.name: TritonBench
entries.use_when: Benchmark representative PyTorch custom operators and compare provider implementations.

entries.name: TorchBench
entries.use_when: Validate compiler or kernel changes against end-to-end PyTorch model workloads.

entries.name: KernelBench
entries.use_when: Evaluate generated or handwritten kernels against PyTorch reference operators across benchmark levels.

entries.name: Kernel Tuner
entries.use_when: Search CUDA/OpenCL/HIP kernel parameter spaces with reproducible tuning records instead of ad hoc loops.

entries.name: Google Benchmark
entries.use_when: Build C++ microbenchmarks around launch, host-side, or integrated extension overhead.

entries.name: CMake and Ninja
entries.use_when: Build native extensions and vendor libraries reproducibly.

entries.name: ccache
entries.use_when: Avoid repeated local C/C++/CUDA compilation during the optimization loop.

entries.name: sccache
entries.use_when: Use local or remote compilation caching for native/CUDA build-heavy projects.

entries.name: pybind11
entries.use_when: Expose C++/CUDA extensions to Python using a mature binding layer.

entries.name: nanobind
entries.use_when: Use a small modern C++/Python binding layer when project compatibility favors it.

entries.name: scikit-build-core
entries.use_when: Package CMake-based Python extensions without custom wheel/build plumbing.

entries.name: TorchTitan
entries.use_when: Run PyTorch-native large-model training experiments instead of rebuilding distributed training infrastructure.

entries.name: Megatron-LM
entries.use_when: Train transformer models with mature tensor/pipeline/context/expert parallel infrastructure.

entries.name: NVIDIA NeMo
entries.use_when: Use NVIDIA's scalable training/post-training stack and integrated kernels rather than building a trainer.

entries.name: DeepSpeed
entries.use_when: Reuse ZeRO, distributed training, inference, and fused extension infrastructure.

entries.name: veRL / HybridFlow
entries.use_when: Run distributed RL post-training and rollout workflows instead of hand-building RL infrastructure.

entries.name: OpenRLHF
entries.use_when: Use a maintained Ray/vLLM-based RLHF and agentic RL framework.

entries.name: Hugging Face TRL
entries.use_when: Use standard SFT/DPO/PPO/GRPO-style post-training APIs for moderate-scale experiments.

entries.name: ROCm HIP toolchain
entries.use_when: Build and diagnose AMD GPU kernels with HIP/ROCm.

entries.name: ROCm Libraries (including Composable Kernel)
entries.use_when: Reuse AMD math/kernel libraries and the maintained Composable Kernel location.

entries.name: ROCm AITER
entries.use_when: Reuse AMD AI tensor-engine kernels for attention, GEMM, MoE, and serving workloads.

entries.name: HipKittens
entries.use_when: Build AMD kernels from reusable tile primitives.

entries.name: oneDNN
entries.use_when: Reuse optimized Intel CPU/GPU deep-learning primitives.

entries.name: CuPy
entries.use_when: Use NumPy/SciPy-compatible GPU arrays, RawKernel/RawModule, and rapid CUDA/HIP kernel experiments.

entries.name: NVIDIA numba-cuda
entries.use_when: Write CUDA kernels in Python when Numba's execution and integration model fits the task.

entries.name: NVIDIA Warp
entries.use_when: Build differentiable GPU kernels for simulation, robotics, geometry, and ML workloads.

entries.name: JAX Pallas and Mosaic GPU
entries.use_when: Implement custom JAX kernels with Pallas/Mosaic while preserving JAX transformations and integration.

entries.name: NVIDIA MathDx (cuBLASDx, cuFFTDx, cuSolverDx)
entries.use_when: Fuse BLAS, FFT, or solver operations inside CUDA kernels through device-callable vendor primitives.

entries.name: NVIDIA cuSPARSELt
entries.use_when: Use NVIDIA's structured-sparse matrix multiplication before authoring custom sparse tensor-core kernels.

entries.name: NVIDIA cuTENSOR
entries.use_when: Use tuned tensor contractions, reductions, and permutations rather than rebuilding general tensor algebra kernels.

entries.name: QuACK CuTe kernels
entries.use_when: Study or reuse a maintained assortment of CuTe DSL kernels before writing equivalent primitives.

entries.name: SageAttention
entries.use_when: Evaluate maintained quantized-attention kernels for language, image, or video inference under the required accuracy contract.

entries.name: SpargeAttention
entries.use_when: Evaluate training-free sparse attention for inference rather than inventing a new sparse execution stack.

entries.name: FlashQLA
entries.use_when: Reuse or benchmark TileLang-based high-performance linear-attention kernels.

entries.name: FlashMoBA
entries.use_when: Reuse optimized Mixture-of-Block-Attention kernels and integration patterns.

entries.name: Block-Sparse-Attention
entries.use_when: Use a maintained mixed-pattern block-sparse attention kernel library.

entries.name: NVIDIA cuEquivariance
entries.use_when: Reuse optimized equivariant tensor-product and structure-model kernels.

entries.name: Mirage Persistent Kernel compiler
entries.use_when: Explore compiling multi-operator LLM regions into persistent mega-kernels when launch/intermediate overhead dominates.

entries.name: BitBLAS
entries.use_when: Consult only for pinned legacy projects or historical mixed-precision GEMM techniques; do not choose by default because the repository is archived.

entries.name: Composable Kernel legacy repository
entries.use_when: Recognize legacy references, then use the maintained ROCm/rocm-libraries location.

entries.name: XeTLA legacy repository
entries.use_when: Recognize pinned Intel legacy projects; do not select as a new default because the repository is archived.

entries.name: Intel Extension for PyTorch legacy repository
entries.use_when: Recognize existing pinned environments and migrate to current Intel/PyTorch-supported paths for new work.
